dedupe_keys.name: zingsa cors network zimbabwe continuously operating gnss reference stations

description: The ZINGSA CORS Network is the national network of continuously operating GNSS reference stations of Zimbabwe, run by the Zimbabwe National Geospatial and Space Agency. The agency describes it as a foundational layer of geospatial accuracy for land administration, construction, mining, agriculture and scientific monitoring: it gives real-time reference for cadastral, engineering and geodetic surveys, GNSS corrections for precision agriculture, continuous observations for geophysical and ionospheric studies, and reference data for roads, mining and urban development. The stations are operational, and ZINGSA is opening them for a six-month free trial from 20 July 2026 to 31 December 2026 for surveyors, engineers, GIS professionals, mining houses and academic institutions, with registration on the Spider Business Center. The page offers a CORS network map, an information flyer and a GIS flyer, and links a CORS portal. Access is free during the trial with registration; terms after the trial and any licence are not stated on the page read. Caveats: the number of stations and the data formats are given in the map and flyers, not on the page. Coverage is Zimbabwe. It supports positioning infrastructure studies and space weather effects on GNSS in southern Africa; related records are CROPOS of Croatia and PositioNZ of New Zealand.
